# Feature: App Host & `yantra ui`

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-065
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

`yantra ui` opens the Yantra app in a Chrome app window, served by a local app host on
`127.0.0.1`. The host is a supervisor, never an executor (memory → Architecture; plan D1–D6):

- **Reads** run in-process.
- **Run-class and mutating commands** launch exactly once each, as detached CLI worker processes.
  At most two app runs hold a slot at a time; the rest queue.
- **Recovery.** After any host crash, a restarted host recovers every invocation and reattaches to
  the runs that are still alive.

The host is safe under the D18 loopback threat model: an exact `Host`/`Origin` canonical origin,
single-use launch codes, per-window capabilities, signed artifact URLs and session expiry.

This feature also ships:

- the `apps/web` skeleton (app shell, top bar, Bindu, navigation, preferences applied), built and
  embedded into the CLI package;
- the `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces` preferences;
- the localhost **security suite**, which is a merge gate from here on.

**Business value.** A non-terminal user can open Yantra with one command and get a window that is
reliable (no invocation launches twice, no run is lost when the host or window dies) and private
(no other web page or loopback service can drive it, and it makes no third-party request). Every
later app feature (FEAT-066 to FEAT-071) builds on this host.

**Milestones (plan §8).**

- **M1, read-only portion:** TASK-001 to TASK-013. These may start once FEAT-062's `read` entries
  and FEAT-061's M1 subset exist.
- **M2, supervisor and launch ownership:** TASK-014 to TASK-019. They need FEAT-063, FEAT-064 and
  FEAT-072.

> **DEVIATION (awaiting confirmation) — window reload.** Plan §7 holds the per-window capability in
> JavaScript memory only, but it does not say what happens when the window reloads (F5, or the D17
> stale-asset reload). Under that rule alone, a reload would lose the session and force the user
> back to the terminal. TASK-003 adds a **resume code**:
>
> - single-use, valid for 60 seconds, and issued only over the authenticated WebSocket;
> - rotated every 45 seconds while the window is connected;
> - kept in that tab's `sessionStorage`, and exchanged through the same `POST /session` path as a
>   launch code.
>
> The capability itself is still never stored. The D17 stale-asset reload does not use storage: it
> navigates to `/#code=<fresh code>`. If this is rejected, drop the `sessionStorage` half. A manual
> reload then shows "Session ended — run `yantra ui` to reopen."

> **Interpretation (not a deviation) — D4 and queued items on restart.** "Queued items start only
> through D11's reservation, never on host restart by themselves" is read as follows:
>
> - Host start never spawns anything directly.
> - After recovery, the normal dequeue loop resumes, and every queued item still passes drift review
>   (TASK-017) and the slot reservation (TASK-014) before a worker spawns.

> **Implementation notes (2026-11-11).** The resume-code DEVIATION above was confirmed by the user.
> Where the code base differed from what this spec assumed:
>
> - **DEVIATION — `ui` registry entry.** FEAT-062 did not add a `ui` entry. TASK-005 adds it
>   (`entries/app.ts`, class `exemption`, decision D15) last in root-help order; the help goldens
>   were recaptured on purpose (one new root line plus the `ui` help files).
> - **DEVIATION — one cookie per browser profile.** Cookies ignore ports, and every app window
>   shares one Chrome profile, so a per-window cookie would let a second window log out the first.
>   `yantra_session` (exact attributes as specified) identifies the profile and may carry several
>   windows; each window keeps its own capability, so window A's cookie with window B's capability
>   is still refused.
> - **DEVIATION — worker launch.** FEAT-064's worker takes `--launch <launch file>` (user text
>   never reaches argv) and offers a `WorkerStartGate` for the claim, not `--invocation-id`.
>   TASK-015 uses that seam; the launch's `result_path` is `invocationResultPath(id)`, so
>   `InvocationResult` is FEAT-064's `WorkerResult`.
> - **DEVIATION — `prefs set` value metadata.** The registry has no per-key value metadata for
>   `prefs set`, so TASK-009 cannot add enum entries there. Validation lives in core
>   (`KEY_VALUE_SCHEMAS`); generated forms need the metadata (TODO, FEAT-070).
> - **DEVIATION — `read.profile`.** `prefs list` returns only stored rows, so a theme set by hand in
>   `profile.yaml` (or left at its default) never appears in `read.prefs.list`. `read.profile`
>   (`yantra profile --json`: effective values, defaults and provenance) is mapped as an M1 reader,
>   and the app applies preferences from it (TASK-011).
> - **No-Host requests.** Node's HTTP parser answers a request without `Host` with 400 before any
>   route runs; that is the refusal for that case (the guard's 421 covers every wrong `Host`).

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> No `.spec-lite/data_model.md` exists. These are file-backed records, not tables. Every persisted
> record is a Zod schema in `@yantra/protocol` with `schema_version`, written atomically through the
> FEAT-072 unique-temp-file helpers (`<file>.<pid>.<random>.tmp` then rename), owner-only (0600 file,
> 0700 directory; on Windows the user-profile default ACL, per §7). Every path is built in
> `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts` (memory → Project Structure).

### Entities & Attributes

- **HostLockRecord** (`<data-dir>/ui/host.lock`, JSON, owner-only). There is one per data directory.
  The FEAT-064 `config data-dir` guard reads it.
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`) — NOT NULL
  - `state` (`'starting' | 'ready'`) — `starting` from acquisition until both listeners are bound
  - `pid` (int > 0), `start_token` (string) — host `ProcessIdentity` (`browser/process-identity.ts`)
  - `port` (int 1–65535 | null) — HTTP port, set when `ready`
  - `control_socket` (string | null) — Unix socket path or Windows named-pipe name (from the
    FEAT-064 socket-address helper)
  - `control_token` (string, 256-bit base64url) — required as the first control-socket message
  - `build_id` (string) — the embedded web build's ID (TASK-012)
  - `yantra_version` (string), `channel_version` (int) — D17
  - `started_at` (ISO-8601), `env_captured_at` (ISO-8601) — D13 environment age, shown by Health
    (FEAT-071)
- **InvocationRecord** (`<data-dir>/ui/invocations/<invocation_id>.json`). Created by exclusive
  create (`wx`); mutated only under `slots.lock`.
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`)
  - `invocation_id` (string, `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$`) — client-generated idempotency key; UNIQUE by
    file name
  - `invocation` (`CommandInvocation {invocation_id, path, argv, cwd}`, FEAT-062) — `cwd` absolute
    and required (D13)
  - `execution_class` (`'run' | 'mutate' | 'exclusive'`) — resolved from the registry for these
    options at submission
  - `state` (`InvocationState`): `queued | reserved | spawning | claimed | running | finished |
never_started | start_unknown | needs_review | discarded`
  - `queued_at` (ISO), `updated_at` (ISO) — FIFO order is by `queued_at`, then `invocation_id`
  - `displayed_effective` (`DisplayedEffective`) — the non-secret effective settings and content
    identities the composer showed at submission (D13); the drift-review baseline
  - `run_id` (string | null) — allocated at `reserved` for `run`-class invocations, and for `resume`
    the existing run's ID
  - `worker` (`{pid, start_token}` | null) — set by the worker's claim; never by the host
  - `review` (`{detected_at, differences: [{key, submitted, current, pinnable}]}` | null) — set on
    `needs_review`
  - `duplicate_risk_acknowledged` (boolean, default `false`) — must be `true` to start a
    `start_unknown` item
  - `result` (`{exit_code, finished_at, reason?: 'owner_lost' | 'busy' | 'refused_claim'}` | null)
- **InvocationResult** (`<data-dir>/ui/invocations/<invocation_id>.result.json`). Written by the
  worker's result transport with exclusive create, before the worker exits.
  - `schema_version`, `invocation_id`
  - `outcome`: either `result {exit_code, envelope}` or `error {exit_code, code, message,
remediation}`, the FEAT-072 result-transport shapes
  - The envelope is capped at 1 MiB. A larger one is replaced by `{truncated: true, bytes}`.
- **DisplayedEffective** (protocol type, embedded above; never persisted on its own)
  - `settings`: `[{key, value, source: 'flag' | 'env' | 'preference' | 'default', env_name?}]` — the
    same entry shape as the FEAT-072 execution receipt; values for options the registry marks
    `secret-input` are rejected
  - `content`: `[{kind: 'workflow' | 'template', path, sha256}]`
- **ResumeCode / LaunchCode** (in host memory only, never persisted)
  - `code_hash` (SHA-256 of 256-bit random) — the code itself is never stored
  - `kind` (`'launch' | 'resume'`), `expires_at` (+60 s), `used` (boolean), `window_id` (resume
    codes only)
- **WindowSession** (in host memory only)
  - `window_id` (random 128-bit), `cookie_id_hash`, `capability_hash` (SHA-256 of the 256-bit
    capability)
  - `created_at`, `absolute_expiry` (+12 h), `disconnected_at` (ISO | null) — expiry is 5 minutes
    after the last socket closes
  - `subscriptions` (set: `runs`, `interventions`, `run:<id>`), `last_attendance_at` (ISO | null)
- **SignedArtifactToken** (stateless; `/a/<payload>.<mac>`)
  - `payload` = base64url JSON `{r: run_id, p: relative_path, w: window_id, e: expiry_epoch_ms}` (+5
    min)
  - `mac` = HMAC-SHA256(host_key, `window_id` ‖ `capability_hash` ‖ payload). The `host_key` is 256
    random bits per host start, in memory only.
- **Profile preferences** (`profile.yaml`, owned by `yantra prefs`; memory → config versus profile)
  - `ui.theme` (`'system' | 'light' | 'dark'`, default `'system'`)
  - `ui.surfaces` (`'glass' | 'solid'`, default `'glass'`)
- **HistoryStore extension** (existing SQLite `history` table; no schema migration)
  - `HistoryListFilter.before?: {startedAt, runId}` — keyset cursor
  - `HistoryStore.changeToken(): Result<number>` — `PRAGMA data_version`, which changes whenever
    another connection commits

### Relationships

- InvocationRecord 0..1 : 1 run directory, via `run_id`. A `resume` invocation references an
  existing run, and the run's exclusive `lease.json` (FEAT-064) is the arbiter.
- InvocationRecord 1 : 0..1 InvocationResult, via `invocation_id`.
- WindowSession 1 : N signed artifact URLs, via `window_id`. Expiring the window invalidates them all.
- HostLockRecord 1 : N WindowSession (in memory). Sessions die with the host.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Slot invariant (D4/D11).** Under `slots.lock`, at most **two** `run`-class records are
  `reserved | spawning | claimed | running` at any moment. An `exclusive`-class record is admitted
  only when that count is 0, and while it is in `reserved..running` no `run` reservation is granted.
  `mutate` holds no slot.
- **State transitions** are a closed table, and any other move throws `InvalidInvocationTransition`:
  - `queued → reserved | needs_review | discarded`
  - `needs_review → queued | discarded`
  - `reserved → spawning | never_started | discarded`
  - `spawning → claimed | never_started | start_unknown`
  - `claimed → running | finished`
  - `running → finished`
  - `never_started → queued | discarded`
  - `start_unknown → queued` (only with `duplicate_risk_acknowledged`) `| discarded`
- **Only the worker writes `worker`**, and only through `claim` (`reserved | spawning → claimed`).
  It is never written by the host.
- **Uniqueness.** Invocation IDs are unique by exclusive create. A repeat submission returns the
  existing record unchanged.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Host state paths, records and the single-instance host lock (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Paths.** Add the `ui` path functions to `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts`, all under
    `dataDir()/ui`.
  - **Schemas.** Add `HostLockRecord`, `InvocationRecord`, `InvocationState`, `InvocationResult`,
    `DisplayedEffective` and `UiOpenResult` to `packages/protocol/src/schemas/app-host.ts`. Each
    field carries a Zod `.describe()`.
  - **`FileHostLock`** in `packages/core/src/app-host/host-lock.ts`:
    - `acquire(identity)` runs inside a short `proper-lockfile` mutex on the lock path. It reads any
      existing record and checks the holder with the injected `ProcessLivenessProbe`:
      - `alive`: throw `HostLockHeldError {record}`, and the caller reuses that host;
      - `dead` (or a mismatched start token): replace the record;
      - `unknown`: throw `HostLockHeldError {uncertain: true}`, and **never reclaim**.

      It then writes a `state: 'starting'` record with a fresh 256-bit `control_token`.

    - `markReady({port, control_socket, build_id})` rewrites the record atomically.
    - `probe()` returns the record plus its liveness verdict.
    - `release()` removes the record only if it still carries this process's identity.

  - Files are 0600 and the directory 0700.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Schema round-trips, plus rejection of a malformed `invocation_id`, a relative `cwd` and a secret
    in `displayed_effective`.
  - A second `acquire` against an `alive` holder throws `HostLockHeldError` carrying the record.
  - A `dead` holder is replaced.
  - A **reused PID** (same PID, different start token) is treated as dead.
  - An `unknown` holder is never reclaimed.
  - `release` by a non-owner leaves the file.
  - `markReady` is atomic: a reader never sees a partial record (simulate a crash between temp write
    and rename).
  - POSIX file modes are 0600/0700 (skipped on Windows).
  - Sandbox through `YANTRA_HOME` and call `resetPathCache()` in `beforeEach`/`afterEach`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the architecture area: the app
      host's process model and its `<data-dir>/ui/` state files.
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/app-host/host-lock.spec.ts`;
  `cd packages/protocol && npx vitest run tests/schemas/app-host.spec.ts`.

### TASK-002: Loopback HTTP server: request guard, security headers and static assets (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Binding.** `AppHost` (`apps/cli/src/ui/host/host.ts`) binds `node:http` to `127.0.0.1` on an
    ephemeral port (`listen(0, '127.0.0.1')`) and never to `0.0.0.0`, `::` or `localhost`.
  - **`request-guard.ts`** runs before every route:
    - rejects any `Host` other than exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>` with 421 and no body (DNS-rebinding
      defense);
    - for every non-GET/HEAD request, requires `Origin` to equal exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
      (403 otherwise);
    - caps request bodies at 1 MiB (413);
    - sends no CORS headers, ever.
  - **Security headers on every response:** - `Content-Security-Policy`: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self';
img-src 'self' blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:<port>;
frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'`; - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; - `X-Frame-Options: DENY`; - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`; - `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`.
  - **`static-assets.ts`** serves `GET /`, `/index.html` and files under `dist/web/assets/`:
    - content-hashed files with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`;
    - `index.html` with `no-store`;
    - unknown paths that look like app routes fall back to `index.html`;
    - asset paths resolve with `realpath` inside the asset root, and any `..` or encoded traversal
      gets 404;
    - `Content-Type` comes from a fixed extension allowlist (`.js`, `.css`, `.woff2`, `.svg`,
      `.png`, `.json`, `.html`).
  - **Missing assets.** If the embedded asset root is missing, `AppHost.start` fails with
    `HostStartError {code: 'assets_missing', remediation: 'Rebuild Yantra (pnpm build).'}`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - A wrong `Host`, an IPv6 `Host`, `localhost:<port>` and a missing `Host` are each rejected.

### TASK-003: Sessions: launch codes, `POST /session`, per-window capabilities and expiry (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `apps/cli/src/ui/host/sessions.ts`: `SessionStore`, with an injected clock and random source.
  - **`issueLaunchCode()`** returns a 256-bit base64url code that is single-use and valid for 60
    seconds. Only its SHA-256 is stored.
  - **`POST /session {code}`** requires the exact Origin (TASK-002). It looks up the code by hash in
    constant time and refuses it if it is used, expired or unknown (401, uniform body
    `{error: 'session_refused'}`). On success it:
    - marks the code used;
    - creates a `WindowSession`;
    - sets the cookie `yantra_session=<random>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` (no `Secure`,
      because the origin is plain http on loopback);
    - returns `{window_id, window_capability, build_id, absolute_expiry}`.
  - **Expiry.** A capability expires 5 minutes after its last WebSocket closes, and 12 hours after
    creation regardless. Expiry also invalidates the window's signed URLs (TASK-010).
  - **Resume code** (see the §1 DEVIATION). Over an authenticated socket, `session.resume_code`
    returns a single-use, 60-second code bound to the same `window_id`. Exchanging it creates a
    **new** capability and revokes the old one.
  - **Never exposed.** Codes, cookies and capabilities never appear in responses other than their own
    issuance, and never in logs (TASK-005 redaction).
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (stepped clock):
  - A code works once, and a second use gets 401.
  - A code at 60 s plus 1 ms gets 401.
  - Capability expiry happens exactly 5 minutes after the last socket closes; a reconnect within
    that window keeps it.
  - The 12-hour absolute expiry holds even while connected.
  - A resume code issued to window A cannot be used after A's capability has expired.
  - Exchanging a resume code revokes the previous capability.
  - Comparisons use `timingSafeEqual`.
  - The cookie attributes are exact.
  - Responses for unknown, used and expired codes are byte-identical.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for safety and privacy: app sessions,
      launch codes and capability expiry.
- **Verify**: `cd apps/cli && npx vitest run tests/ui/host/sessions.spec.ts`.

### TASK-004: WebSocket JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint with `auth`, limits and the build-ID handshake (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Upgrade.** `apps/cli/src/ui/host/rpc-server.ts` uses `ws` with `noServer: true`. The HTTP
    `upgrade` handler applies the TASK-002 `Host` and exact-`Origin` checks and requires a valid
    session cookie before calling `handleUpgrade`. Failures get a raw 403 and the socket is
    destroyed.
  - **Limits.** `maxPayload` is 1 MiB.
  - **Auth.** The first message must be `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"auth","params":{"window_capability"}}`.
    The capability must match the cookie's window. Otherwise the socket closes with code 4401 and no
    reply. Any other first message, or none within 5 seconds, also closes it.
  - **Dispatcher.** A typed method registry: method name, then params schema, then handler, then
    result schema. Params and results are validated with the `app-rpc.ts` Zod schemas.
  - **Errors.** JSON-RPC errors use the standard codes (-32700, -32600, -32601, -32602) and app
    codes: -32001 `unauthorized`, -32002 `busy`, -32003 `not_allowed`, -32004 `not_found`, -32005
    `too_large`, -32006 `needs_confirmation`.
    - Every error's `data` is `{code, message, remediation?}`, saying what happened and one next
      step (memory → Coding Standards).
  - **First method, `host.hello {build_id, channel_version}`.** It returns `{build_id,
channel_version, yantra_version, server_time}`. The `host.build` notification repeats the build
    ID on every connect (D17 stale assets).
  - **Heartbeat.** The server pings every 15 seconds and terminates a socket that misses two pongs.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - An upgrade without a cookie, with a foreign `Origin` or with a rebinding `Host` is refused.
  - The first message must be `auth`, and the wrong capability for the cookie closes with 4401.
  - A cookie from window A with window B's capability is refused.
  - A frame over 1 MiB closes the socket.
  - An unknown method returns -32601, and bad params return -32602 with a remediation.
  - A batch request is answered per item.
  - `host.hello` returns the host's build ID.
  - An expired capability closes any open socket.
  - A request ID echo is preserved.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the protocol spec: the app ↔ host
      JSON-RPC methods and error codes (derived from the Zod descriptions).
- **Verify**: `cd apps/cli && npx vitest run tests/ui/host/rpc-server.spec.ts`.
- **Depends on**: TASK-002, TASK-003

### TASK-005: Host entry, control socket, host log and `yantra ui --print` / `--json` (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Host entry.** `apps/cli/src/ui-host.ts` is the detached host entry. It:
    1. acquires `FileHostLock`;
    2. records `env_captured_at`;
    3. opens `host-log.ts`: a Pino file logger at `hostLogPath()`, rotated once to `host.log.1`
       when over 10 MiB at start, with `redact` paths for every code, cookie, capability, token,
       signed URL and `secret` key;
    4. binds HTTP (TASK-002) and the **control socket** (`control-socket.ts`, using FEAT-064's frame
       codec);
    5. calls `markReady`.
  - **Control socket.** The first message must be `hello {control_token, channel_version}`; anything
    else is closed without a reply. Methods are `launch_code.issue` → `{code, expires_at}` and
    `host.status` → `{pid, port, build_id, yantra_version, started_at}`.
  - **Shutdown.** `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` stop listening, close sockets and release the lock. Workers are
    never signalled (D6).
  - **The command.** `apps/cli/src/commands/ui.ts` (`yantra ui [--print] [--json]`, bound through the
    registry):
    1. `FileHostLock.probe()`.
    2. **If no live host:** spawn `dist/ui-host.js` detached, shell-free, with an explicit argv
       array, `stdio: 'ignore'`, `windowsHide: true`, and the CLI's own `process.env` and an
       explicit `cwd` of the data directory. Then wait up to 10 seconds for `state: 'ready'`.
    3. Connect to the control socket, authenticate, and issue a launch code.
    4. Build the URL `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#code=<code>`.
  - **`--print`** prints the URL and exits 0. **`--json`** emits `UiOpenResult {schemaVersion: 1,
url, port, hostPid, reused}`.
  - **Exit codes.** 3 for environment failures, each with a remediation:
    - lock held by an `unknown` identity;
    - host failed to become ready (the remediation names `host.log`);
    - bind failure;
    - assets missing.

    1 for validation. The handler follows the FEAT-072 seams: no `process.exit` and no direct stdout.

  - **Version mismatch.** When a reused host's `yantra_version` differs from the CLI's, a human-mode
    notice goes to stderr: "The running app is Yantra X; close the app and run `yantra ui` to use
    Y." `--json` stays unchanged.

  - A second `ui --print` reuses the host (`reused: true`) and issues a different code.
  - `--json` matches `UiOpenResult` exactly.
  - Two concurrent `yantra ui` invocations start exactly one host; the loser reuses it.
  - An `unknown` lock holder gives exit 3 with a remediation.
  - A host that never becomes ready gives exit 3 naming `host.log`.
  - An unauthenticated or wrong-token control client gets no reply.
  - The spawn arguments contain no code or token.
  - A **canary scan of `host.log`**, after issuing codes, a session, signed URLs and a
    `secret`-named field, finds none of them.
  - The handler never calls `process.exit` (FEAT-072 lint).

### TASK-008: Change detection: `runs.subscribe` without reloads (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`ChangeFeed`** (`apps/cli/src/ui/host/change-feed.ts`) combines three sources:
    1. a **lease scan** of `runs/*/lease.json` (presence and heartbeat) every 2 seconds;
    2. polling `HistoryStore.changeToken()` (`PRAGMA data_version` on a long-lived connection) every
       2 seconds;

    or `prefs.changed`, sent to windows subscribed through `runs.subscribe`.

    (for example `EMFILE`, or an unsupported filesystem) degrade to polling, and that degradation is
    logged once.

  - Five rapid changes yield one notification.
  - A watcher error falls back to polling.
  - There is no polling with zero subscribers.
  - A `profile.yaml` edit produces `prefs.changed`.

### TASK-010: Signed artifact URLs `/a/<signed>` with a public allowlist (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Issuing.** `artifact.url {run_id, path}` (RPC) checks the path against the artifact policy and
    returns `/a/<payload>.<mac>`, signed as in §2 and expiring after 5 minutes.
  - **`GET /a/<signed>`** requires, in order: the exact `Host`, a valid session cookie whose window
    matches `w`, a constant-time MAC check, an unexpired `e`, and a live window. Then it resolves
    `realpath(join(runsRoot(), run_id, path))`, which must remain inside that run directory.
  - **Never served (§7):** `lease.json`, `reconcile.lock`, `decisions/`, `*.tmp`, sockets,
    `host.lock`, `invocations/` and browser profiles. These are refused before any filesystem read.
  - **Allowlist seam.** `ArtifactPolicy.isPublic(relativePath)` is the seam. FEAT-066 owns the full
    registry-backed allowlist. Until it lands, the default allows only `captures/**/*.{png,jpg,jpeg}`
    and `report.md`. Everything else is denied.
  - **Response.** `Content-Type` comes from the extension allowlist, with `nosniff`. Markdown, HTML
    and anything not an image are served with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, and `Cache-Control`
    is `no-store`.
  - **Denials** return a uniform 404, and their count is logged.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - A valid URL serves the file.
  - A URL signed for window A fails with window B's cookie.
  - A URL fails one millisecond after expiry.
  - Changing one byte of the payload or MAC fails.
  - A traversal (`../`, an absolute path, a symlink that escapes the run directory) gets 404.
  - Each denied name gets 404 even if an allowlist mistakenly includes it (the denylist wins).
  - An HTML file is served as an attachment.
  - Expiring a window kills its outstanding URLs.
  - The host key changes across host restarts, so old URLs fail.

      artifacts the app can fetch and how the URLs are bound.

- [ ] **Implementation**:

    `host.hello`.

### TASK-013: Localhost security suite (merge gate) and the no-third-party-request check (M1)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **The suite.** `apps/cli/tests/ui/security/` starts a real host on a sandboxed `YANTRA_HOME` and
    covers every §10 security case:
    - a missing, replayed or expired launch code;
    - a missing, replayed or expired capability (5 minutes after disconnect, and 12 hours absolute,
      on a stepped clock);
    - a session cookie presented without a capability;
    - a cookie from a page on another loopback port (a second `node:http` server on 127.0.0.1
      issuing a cross-port `fetch` and WebSocket upgrade);
    - a foreign `Origin`, a rebinding `Host` and a cross-site form POST to `/session`;
    - an unauthenticated control socket;
    - fetching `lease.json`, `host.lock`, `invocations/`, `decisions/` and `reconcile.lock` through
      static, signed and traversal paths;
    - **outbound canary scans.** Plant a canary secret and canary codes, then scan every host→app
      message, HTTP response body and header, and `host.log`.
  - **Run-socket gap.** An unauthenticated run socket is FEAT-064's acceptance; this suite re-runs
    that assertion against a host-spawned worker once TASK-015 lands.
  - **E2E.** `e2e/app-host.spec.ts` uses puppeteer-core and the built CLI. It runs `yantra ui
--print`, opens the URL, waits for `connected`, and: - asserts that **no request leaves `127.0.0.1:<port>`** (request interception records every URL); - asserts that **no CSP violation** is reported (`securitypolicyviolation` listener); - asserts that the URL fragment is gone; - runs `axe-core` on the shell, with no violations.
  - **Merge gate.** Tag the suite so CI runs it on Windows, macOS and Linux.

### TASK-014: Launch ownership core: invocation records, slot lock, reservation and worker claim (M2)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`FileInvocationStore`** in `packages/core/src/app-host/invocation-store.ts`:
    - `create(record)` uses exclusive create (`wx`). On `EEXIST` it returns the existing record (the
      idempotency rule, D11).
    - **Every mutation** runs under `proper-lockfile` on `slotsLockPath()` (retries 0, bounded wait
      of 2 seconds, then `SlotLockBusyError`) and writes with the FEAT-072 unique-temp helper.
    - `reserve(id, allocateRunId)` moves `queued → reserved` only while the §2 slot invariant holds.
      It allocates `run_id` (the existing ID for `resume`) and returns `{reserved: false, position}`
      otherwise.
    - `markSpawning(id)`.
    - `claim(id, identity)` is the worker's first action. It moves `reserved | spawning → claimed`
      and records `worker`. From `never_started` or `discarded` it throws `ClaimRefusedError`, after
      which the worker exits with no side effects. Any other state throws
      `InvalidInvocationTransition`.
    - `markRunning`, `finish(id, result)`, `discard`, `requeue` and `setReview`.
    - `writeResult(id, outcome)` (exclusive create) and `readResult`.
  - **Transitions.** The §2 table is the only legal set.
  - **`recoverInvocations`** (`invocation-recovery.ts`, under the lock):
    - unclaimed `reserved | spawning` → `never_started`;
    - `claimed | running` with a worker the probe calls `alive` → returned as `attach`;
    - `dead` → returned as `reconcile` (the caller runs FEAT-064 `reconcileRun`, then
      `finish(..., {reason: 'owner_lost'})`);
    - `unknown` → `start_unknown`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Ten concurrent `create` calls with one ID make one file, and all return the same record.
  - Twenty concurrent `reserve` calls (in separate processes through `child_process.fork`) never
    exceed two `run` slots.
  - `mutate` reservations do not consume slots.
  - An `exclusive` reservation waits for zero runs and blocks new runs.
  - A claim after `never_started` throws `ClaimRefusedError`.
  - A claim and a recovery racing under the lock end in exactly one of `claimed` or
    `never_started`.
  - Every illegal transition throws.
  - The recovery verdict table is covered for alive, dead, unknown and reused-PID cases.
  - A busy lock surfaces `SlotLockBusyError`, never a silent write.

      ownership (invocation states, the slot lock, the worker claim).

tests/app-host/invocation-recovery.spec.ts`.

### TASK-015: Supervisor: `command.invoke`, the queue, worker spawn, cancel and results (M2)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **`command.invoke {invocation, displayed_effective}`** (`supervisor.ts`): 1. Parse `invocation` through FEAT-062 (registry path, argv validity). The `cwd` must be
    absolute. 2. Resolve the execution class for these options. Refusals use `not_allowed`, with the reason
    and the right surface: - `read`: use `read.<name>`; - `in-process-secure`: use `secret.*` (FEAT-071); - `adapter`: no adapter registered yet; - `exemption`: for example `ui` or `config data-dir`, refused with the written D15 steps. 3. Create the record (`queued`), then try `reserve`. On success: `markSpawning`, then spawn
    through the FEAT-064 spawn helper (detached, shell-free, `[execPath, dist/worker.js,
'--invocation-id', id]`, the `cwd` from the invocation, the host's environment captured at
    start (D13), no inherited stdio, `windowsHide`). 4. Return `{invocation_id, state, position?, run_id?}`.
  - **Repeated submissions.** The same `invocation_id` returns the current record's state and never
    spawns.
  - **Worker side** (`apps/cli/src/ui/worker-claim.ts`, called by the FEAT-064 worker entry when
    `--invocation-id` is given):
    1. `claim` first, and on `ClaimRefusedError` exit 0 with no other effect;
    2. run the invocation through the FEAT-072 worker adapter with the pre-allocated `run_id`;
    3. `markRunning` once the lease exists;
    4. on completion, `writeResult`, then `finish`.
  - **Dequeue loop.** Triggered by `finish`, a change-feed lease removal, and a 2-second tick. It
    takes FIFO `queued` items through drift review (TASK-017), then `reserve`.
  - **Cancel.** `command.cancel {invocation_id}`:
    - `queued | needs_review | never_started | start_unknown` → `discarded`;
    - `reserved | spawning` → `discarded` under the lock, so a late claim is refused;
    - `claimed | running` → `cancel` over the run socket (FEAT-064). If the process is still alive
      after 10 seconds, force-terminate the identity-verified process tree, **always followed by
      reconciliation** (the §8 reliability matrix). A `mutate` worker without a socket is
      force-terminated after 10 seconds.
  - **Queue RPCs.**
    - `queue.list` returns records with positions.
    - `queue.start {invocation_id, acknowledge_duplicate_risk?}` serves `never_started`, and serves
      `start_unknown` only with `acknowledge_duplicate_risk: true`; otherwise it returns -32006
      `needs_confirmation` with the possible-duplicate-effects warning.
    - `queue.discard`.
  - **Notifications.** Each state change sends `invocation.changed {record summary}`, and each result
    sends `invocation.result {invocation_id, outcome}`, both to subscribed windows.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (fake spawner, fake run socket, stepped clock):
  - A `run` invoke spawns once and returns `run_id`.
  - Three `run` invokes leave the third `queued` at position 1, and it starts when one finishes.
  - A repeat of the same ID after a lost response returns the same state with no second spawn.
  - A `read` invoke gets `not_allowed` naming `read.list`.
  - `ui` gets `not_allowed`.
  - Cancelling a `reserved` item causes the worker's claim to be refused.
  - A graceful cancel sends `cancel`, and force follows at 10 s with reconciliation called.
  - `start_unknown` without acknowledgement gets -32006.
  - The spawn argv contains no secret and is shell-free.
  - A worker refusing its claim leaves no run directory.
  - The result file feeds `invocation.result`.

### TASK-016: Host-start recovery, run reattach and `run.subscribe` relay (M2)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **On host start** (after `markReady`):
    1. run `recoverInvocations`;
    2. for `reconcile` verdicts, call FEAT-064 `reconcileRun`, then `finish`;
    3. scan `runs/*/lease.json` for live, identity-verified owners;
    4. resume the dequeue loop.
  - **`run-relay.ts`** attaches lazily to a run's socket when the first window calls `run.subscribe
{run_id, from_seq}`: - authenticates with the lease's run token; - sends `hello {channel_version, capabilities}`; - on an incompatible version, marks the run `live_unavailable`, sends `run.channel {run_id,
state: 'live_unavailable', worker_version}`, and **never aborts the worker** (D17); - otherwise sends `subscribe {from_seq: min over windows}` and forwards `run.event {run_id, seq,
event}` to each window from its own `from_seq`, deduplicating by `seq`.
  - **Detach.** The relay detaches when the last window unsubscribes. A worker without a socket
    (finished) is served from `run-events.jsonl` replay only.
  - **Worker not responding.** No heartbeat for 30 seconds sends `run.channel {state:
'not_responding'}` and logs that once.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Two windows with different `from_seq` each receive a gap-free sequence without duplicates.
  - An event emitted during replay is delivered once.
  - A previous-`channel_version` worker fixture yields `live_unavailable`, and no `cancel` is ever
    sent.
  - A finished run replays from file.
  - The 30-second heartbeat gap emits `not_responding` once.
  - Recovery reconciles a dead `claimed` record exactly once, even with two hosts racing (the second
    is refused by the host lock).

### TASK-017: Queue drift review (D13)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Re-resolution.** Before `reserve`, `drift-review.ts` re-resolves the queued invocation's
    effective settings read-only through the FEAT-072 settings resolver. It also recomputes workflow
    and template SHA-256 identities, then compares the result with `displayed_effective`.
  - **On any difference:** `setReview` moves the item to `needs_review` with `differences[]`:
    - a key, the submitted value and the current value;
    - `pinnable`: true when the registry maps the key to a flag on this command.

    It then sends `invocation.changed`. The Inbox surfaces this in FEAT-068.

  - **`queue.resolve_review {invocation_id, choice}`:**
    - `current`: requeue as is;
    - `submitted`: rewrite `invocation.argv` to pin each differing value as an explicit flag.
      **Unavailable** (`not_allowed`, with the reason) when any difference is not pinnable, or when a
      workflow or template content identity changed;
    - `discard`.
  - **Missing workflow.** A workflow that no longer exists makes the item `needs_review`, with
    `current: null`.

  - No change gives a direct reserve.
  - An edited workflow file gives a content difference, and `submitted` is unavailable.
  - `submitted` pins flags, and `CommandInvocation.format` shows them.
  - An env-sourced value reports the env var **name**, never its value.
  - A missing workflow gives `needs_review`.
  - `discard` is terminal.

### TASK-018: Attendance relay (D5) and idle exit (M2)

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Subscription.** `interventions.subscribe` marks a window as an intervention subscriber and
    forwards `intervention_raised` and `intervention_resolved` `RunEvent`s from attached runs.
    FEAT-068 owns the `Intervention` model and the answers.
  - **Heartbeat.** The app sends `attendance.heartbeat` every 10 seconds while subscribed.
  - **`attendance.ts`.** A window counts as attending only with a live, authenticated socket, an
    intervention subscription and a heartbeat within 30 seconds.
    - The count goes to every attached worker as `attendance {count}` on change, on attach, and
      every 10 seconds.
    - **Zero windows means count 0**, whatever the queue or host state (D5).
  - **`idle-exit.ts`.** When no window is connected and no invocation is `reserved`, `spawning` or
    `queued`, a 10-minute timer starts; any connection or new invocation cancels it.
    - On expiry the host shuts down gracefully (TASK-005). `claimed` and `running` workers do not
      block exit and are never touched (§8 reliability matrix).
  - **Worker-side recording.** `attendance_changed` and `attendance_ceiling_expired` in
    `runtime.jsonl` are written by the worker (FEAT-068). The host logs only count changes.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (stepped clock):
  - One subscribed window with fresh heartbeats gives count 1. A missed heartbeat at 30 seconds
    plus 1 ms gives 0.
  - A connected but unsubscribed window gives 0.
  - **A live host with zero windows and a non-empty queue sends 0.**
  - A newly attached worker immediately receives the current count.
  - The idle timer fires at exactly 10 minutes with only `running` invocations, and does not fire
    with a `queued` one.
  - A reconnect during the idle period cancels the timer.
  - Shutdown never signals a worker.

### TASK-019: Launch-ownership evidence (§10 B1) and the M2 end-to-end run

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Evidence suite.** `apps/cli/tests/ui/launch-ownership/` runs against a real host process and a
    fake-but-real worker binary. The worker is the FEAT-064 entry running a fixture command that
    sleeps and writes a marker file once per execution. It uses fault-injection points (an env-gated
    `YANTRA_TEST_FAULT=<point>` that kills the process at that point, **compiled only into the test
    fixture**, never into `src/`). The cases:
    - simultaneous submissions of different IDs (never more than two running);
    - a lost RPC response followed by a retry of the same ID;
    - a host kill before spawn, after spawn but before the claim, after the claim but before the
      lease, and after completion but before the response;
    - two concurrent `resume` invocations of one run (exactly one owns the lease, and the other ends
      `busy`).

    Each case asserts exactly one marker per invocation, at most two `reserved-or-running` slots at
    every observation, and a valid final state (`finished`, `never_started` or `start_unknown`).

  - **M2 e2e.** `e2e/app-host.spec.ts`:
    1. `yantra ui --print`;
    2. a window connects;
    3. `command.invoke` of `research --no-llm <fixture query>` against the local fixture server;
    4. the window follows `run.event` to the terminal outcome;
    5. **kill the host mid-run**; the worker keeps running; `yantra ui --print` starts a new host,
       which reattaches; the window replays with no gaps and sees completion.

    This runs in the `LLM_PROVIDER=none` dimension.

  - **Cross-platform.** All of this runs on Windows, macOS and Linux CI.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth.** Everything that reaches the host is authenticated at its boundary.
  - **HTTP:** the exact `Host` everywhere, and the exact `Origin` on mutations (TASK-002).
  - **Sessions:** a single-use launch or resume code, then cookie **plus** per-window capability on
    every RPC, and cookie plus a window-bound signature on every artifact URL (TASK-003, TASK-004,
    TASK-010).
  - **Sockets:** a token-first control socket (TASK-005) and token-first run sockets (FEAT-064).
  - **Out of scope (D18):** same-user code and physical access.
  - **Residual risk:** the launch code appears in the Chrome process's argv (`--app=<url>`), which
    other OS users can read on some systems. It is single-use, valid for 60 seconds, and consumed on
    the window's first load. A TODO entry tracks hardening.
- **Error Handling.**
  - **CLI exit codes** follow memory: 0 opened or printed, 1 validation, 3 environment (no
    Chromium, bind failure, lock contention, assets missing, `busy`).
  - **Typed errors.** Host and core failures are custom `Error` subclasses with an actionable
    `remediation`: `HostLockHeldError`, `HostStartError`, `InvalidInvocationTransition`,
    `ClaimRefusedError`, `SlotLockBusyError`.
  - **RPC errors** carry `{code, message, remediation?}` and say what actually happened.
  - **Per-item failure.** A failing reader or attach fails that item, never the host.
  - **Busy locks** are explicit and never silent (D14).
- **Logging.** `host.log` (Pino) records the §11 events:
  - host start and stop, with `env_captured_at`;
  - invocation transitions (invocation ID, run ID, class);
  - worker claim and exit;
  - attach and reattach, with handshake versions;
  - reconciliation decisions;
  - drift reviews;
  - lock-busy responses;
  - security rejections, as counts with the rejected `Origin` host.

  It **never** records launch or resume codes, cookies, capabilities, tokens, signed URLs, secret
  values or frames. Pino `redact` enforces this, and the TASK-005 and TASK-013 canary scans prove
  it. Individual heartbeats are not logged, and "not responding" is logged once.

- **Consent and safety.** The host decides nothing. Interventions are only relayed here (FEAT-068
  owns decisions). The attendance count never treats host liveness as attendance (D5).
- **Zero-LLM boundaries.** The daemon is untouched (D1). The host opens no model session; agentic
  work happens only inside workers.
- **Accessibility.** The shell uses Drshya primitives, focus is visible, connection changes are
  announced through a polite live region without stealing focus, and `axe-core` is clean
  (TASK-013).
